request.title: Automate the Bottleneck, Not the Demo
request.topic: How a software founder should choose the first workflow to automate

beats.text: The best AI automation is usually the least impressive demo and the easiest line item to measure.
Teams often automate the task that looks futuristic while the real bottleneck still makes people wait every single day.
That creates more software to supervise without removing enough cost, delay, or repeated mistakes.
So rank the workflow before you build it.
First, count how often the task happens.
Next, measure how long a person or customer waits for it.
Then, decide whether the output can be checked from a receipt instead of someone's opinion.
For example, a lead handoff lets you measure the incoming lead, the response time, the routing decision, and whether the meeting was booked.
If a workflow is frequent, slow, and easy to verify, it is a strong automation candidate. If one of those is missing, keep looking.
Start with one repeated task today and score it on frequency, waiting time, and proof.

script.transcript: The best AI automation is usually the least impressive demo and the easiest line item to measure. Teams often automate the task that looks futuristic while the real bottleneck still makes people wait every single day. That creates more software to supervise without removing enough cost, delay, or repeated mistakes. So rank the workflow before you build it. First, count how often the task happens. Next, measure how long a person or customer waits for it. Then, decide whether the output can be checked from a receipt instead of someone's opinion. For example, a lead handoff lets you measure the incoming lead, the response time, the routing decision, and whether the meeting was booked. If a workflow is frequent, slow, and easy to verify, it is a strong automation candidate. If one of those is missing, keep looking. Start with one repeated task today and score it on frequency, waiting time, and proof.
